questions.question: The sum of five numbers is 655. The average of the first two numbers is 77 and the third number is 102. Find the average of the remaining two numbers.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Sum of remaining 2 numbers** = 655 − (2 × 77) − 102

⇒ 655 − 154 − 102 = 399

**Average** = 399 ÷ 2 = 199.5

**∴ The correct answer is 199.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total sum of **5 numbers** = 655

Average of **first 2 numbers** = 77

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c0570caa88ed236cab3cd6c81ed851605b12cc688458f0244372d780c1834135.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of first 2 numbers = Average × Count = 77 × 2 = 154

⇒ Sum of first 3 numbers = (Sum of first 2) + (3rd number) = 154 + 102 = 256

⇒ Sum of remaining 2 numbers = (Total sum) − (Sum of first 3) = 655 − 256 = 399

⇒ Average of remaining 2 numbers = (Sum of remaining 2) ÷ 2

⇒ Average = 399 ÷ 2 = 199.5

**∴ The correct answer is 199.5.**

The **Arithmetic Mean** or average is the ratio of the sum of all values to the total number of values. Formula: **Avg = Total Sum ÷ n**.

If the average and the number of observations are known, the total sum is calculated as: **Sum = Average × Number of terms**.

questions.question: Which characteristic of the CPU determines how many instructions it can process per second?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Clock Speed**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Clock speed** is the rate at which a CPU executes instructions, measured in **Hertz (Hz)**, typically in **gigahertz (GHz)** for modern processors.
 
• It determines how many **cycles per second** the CPU can perform, directly impacting the number of instructions it can process per second.
 
• Higher clock speeds generally lead to **faster processing** and improved performance in computational tasks.
 
• Clock speed is a critical factor in determining the overall **performance** of a CPU, especially for tasks requiring high computational power.
 
• Modern CPUs also utilize techniques like **turbo boost** to temporarily increase clock speed for demanding applications.
 
• However, clock speed alone doesn’t determine performance; it must be combined with other factors like **core count** and **architecture efficiency**.
 
• A CPU with a higher clock speed but fewer cores may perform better for single-threaded tasks, while multi-core CPUs are better for multi-threaded applications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Power Consumption**__

 __
 
• **Power consumption** refers to the amount of electrical energy the CPU uses during its operation.
 
• It has an impact on **heat generation** and the need for cooling solutions but does not directly determine the number of instructions a CPU can process per second.
 
• Efficient CPUs balance power consumption and performance for tasks like mobile devices and laptops.
 
 
 
• **Cache Size**__
 __
 
• **Cache size** refers to the amount of high-speed memory available on the CPU for storing frequently used data.
 
• A larger cache can improve **performance** by reducing the need to access slower main memory, but it doesn’t directly define how many instructions can be processed per second.
 
• It plays a crucial role in reducing **latency** and improving data retrieval speeds.
 
 
 
• **Number of Registers**__
 
 
• The **number of registers** refers to the small amount of memory within the CPU used to store data temporarily during execution.
 
• While registers are essential for efficient data processing, their count doesn’t directly determine the CPU's ability to process instructions per second.
 
• Registers are vital for tasks like **arithmetic operations** and **instruction decoding**.

questions.question: If you want your audience to NOT see your notes in the MS PowerPoint 365 slides, which view should you use during slide show?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Presenter View**__.

__
 
• **Presenter View** is a feature in **MS PowerPoint 365** that allows the presenter to see notes and other tools on their screen while the audience only sees the slide presentation.
 
• In **Presenter View**, the presenter has access to **tools** such as a timer, navigation controls, and the ability to view their speaker notes privately.
 
• This mode is particularly useful for maintaining a **professional presentation flow** while keeping key notes and details for the presenter out of the audience's view.
 
• **Presenter View** typically requires a dual-monitor setup, where one monitor displays the presentation for the audience, and the other monitor shows the **notes and controls for the presenter.**
 
• It enhances the **engagement** and **confidence** of the presenter by providing a clear view of their notes and upcoming slides.
 
• To enable **Presenter View**, go to the **Slide Show** tab, and then check the box labeled "**Use Presenter View**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Outline View**__

 __
 
• The **Outline View** in PowerPoint shows the **text content of slides** in an outline format.
 
• It is commonly used for editing and organizing content but is not suitable for hiding notes during a presentation.
 
 
 
• **Slide Show View**__
 __
 
• The **Slide Show View** is used to display slides to the audience in full-screen mode.
 
• While this view does not show notes to the audience, it also does not allow the presenter to view their notes privately, unlike **Presenter View**.
 
 
 
• **Reading View**__
 
 
• The **Reading View** displays the presentation in a **windowed format** and is useful for reviewing the presentation on a single screen.
 
• It does not provide tools for presenting with notes hidden from the audience.

questions.question: Which of the following brings winter rainfall to northern plains of India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Western disturbances**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Western disturbances** are extratropical storms originating in the **Mediterranean region**.
 
• They travel eastward and bring **winter rainfall** to the **northern plains of India**, particularly in **Punjab, Haryana, and western Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• These disturbances are caused due to the westerly winds in the upper atmosphere, which carry moisture from the **Mediterranean Sea**, the **Atlantic Ocean**, and sometimes even from the **Caspian Sea**.
 
• The rainfall brought by these disturbances is crucial for the **rabi crops**, especially **wheat**, in northern India.
 
• They usually occur during the **winter months**, from December to February, though they can sometimes extend into early March.
 
• The interaction of Western disturbances with the Himalayas often leads to snowfall in the **higher altitudes** and rainfall in the plains.
 
• This phenomenon plays a significant role in maintaining the **climate balance** in the region by lowering temperatures and providing moisture.
 
• Western disturbances are also responsible for causing **cold waves** in northern India during winters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Norwesters**__

 __
 
• **Norwesters**, also called **Kalbaisakhi** in India, are thunderstorms that occur during the **pre-monsoon season**, mainly in **eastern India**, such as West Bengal, Assam, and Odisha.
 
• These storms are characterized by strong winds, heavy rainfall, and sometimes hailstorms, but they are not responsible for winter rainfall.
 
 
 
• **Bay of Bengal cyclones**__
 __
 
• **Bay of Bengal cyclones** are tropical cyclones that form over the **Bay of Bengal**, typically during the **pre-monsoon (April-May)** and **post-monsoon (October-November)** seasons.
 
• These cyclones are responsible for heavy rainfall in the eastern coastal states of India but do not impact the winter rainfall in northern plains.
 
 
 
• **Easterlies**__
 
 
• **Easterlies** are trade winds that blow from the east to the west in the **tropical regions**.
 
• They are associated with the monsoon season in India and do not contribute to winter rainfall in the northern plains.

Net Profit% = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100, where a = **Markup%** and b = **Discount%** (negative).

Net Profit% = 64 − 25 − (64 × 25) ÷ 100

Net Profit% = 39 − (1600 ÷ 100)

Net Profit% = 39 − 16 = 23%.

Since the result is positive, it is a **23% gain**.

**∴ The correct answer is 23% gain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → **Markup%** = 64%, **Discount%** = 25%.
Formulas: MP = CP × (100 + Markup%) ÷ 100 | SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100 | Gain% = (SP − CP) ÷ CP × 100
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/520aedd58a09537c668b0cdf096f545a90f6519bc1c077023ab3995b57099327.png] 
⇒ Let **Cost Price (CP)** = 100.
⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 64% of 100 = 164.
⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 164 − 25% of 164 = 164 − (164 ÷ 4) = 164 − 41 = 123.
⇒ **Gain** = SP − CP = 123 − 100 = 23.
⇒ **Gain%** = (23 ÷ 100) × 100 = 23%.

**∴ The correct answer is 23% gain.**

questions.question: If the equations x² + 3x + 2 = 0 { and } ax² + bx + c = 0 have both roots in in common, then which of the following is NOT true?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For two quadratic equations to have **both roots in common**, the ratio of their coefficients must be equal: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂.

Comparing x² + 3x + 2 = 0 and ax² + bx + c = 0, we get: a/1 = b/3 = c/2 = k.

Let k = 1, then **a = 1, b = 3, c = 2**.

Substituting these in Option 1: 4(1) = 2(2) + 2(3) ⇒ 4 = 10, which is **NOT true**.

All other options (2, 3, and 4) satisfy these values: 4(1) − 2(3) + 2 = 0; 1 + 2 = 3; 1 − 3 + 2 = 0.

**∴ The correct answer is 4a = 2c + 2b.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Equations:**

Equation 1: x² + 3x + 2 = 0

Equation 2: ax² + bx + c = 0

**Step 1: Solve for the roots of Equation 1.**

⇒ x² + 2x + x + 2 = 0

⇒ x(x + 2) + 1(x + 2) = 0

⇒ (x + 1)(x + 2) = 0

⇒ The roots are **x = −1** and **x = −2**.

**Step 2: Substitute the roots into Equation 2.**

Since both roots are common, −1 and −2 must satisfy ax² + bx + c = 0.

⇒ For x = −1: a(−1)² + b(−1) + c = 0 ⇒ **a − b + c = 0** (Option 4 is True).

⇒ From a − b + c = 0, we get **a + c = b** (Option 3 is True).

⇒ For x = −2: a(−2)² + b(−2) + c = 0 ⇒ **4a − 2b + c = 0** (Option 2 is True).

**Step 3: Evaluate Option 1.**

⇒ From the condition of proportionality for common roots: b = 3a and c = 2a.

⇒ Checking 4a = 2c + 2b ⇒ 4a = 2(2a) + 2(3a) ⇒ 4a = 4a + 6a ⇒ 4a = 10a.

⇒ Since a ≠ 0 (for a quadratic equation), 4a ≠ 10a.

**∴ The correct answer is 4a = 2c + 2b.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Condition for Both Roots Common

For two quadratic equations a₁x² + b₁x + c₁ = 0 and a₂x² + b₂x + c₂ = 0, if both roots are common, then a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂.

Condition for One Root Common

If only one root is common, then (c₁a₂ − c₂a₁)² = (a₁b₂ − a₂b₁)(b₁c₂ − b₂c₁).

Relationship Between Roots and Coefficients

For ax² + bx + c = 0, Sum of roots (α+β) = −b/a and Product of roots (αβ) = c/a.

Nature of Roots

Determined by the Discriminant D = b² − 4ac. Roots are real and equal if D = 0, and complex if D < 0.</p

questions.question: Dholavira site of Indus Valley Civilization is best known for which of the following practices?

__
 
• **Dholavira** is one of the most prominent archaeological sites of the **Indus Valley Civilization**, located in the present-day state of **Gujarat, India**.
 
• The site is best known for its advanced **water conservation system**, which includes a network of **step wells, reservoirs, and channels**.
 
• This sophisticated water management system demonstrates the **engineering expertise** of the Indus Valley people in addressing water scarcity in a semi-arid region.
 
• **Dholavira's water system** ensured the storage and efficient use of water throughout the year, especially during dry periods.

 __

questions.question: Find the smallest number by which 2527 must be multiplied to make it a perfect square.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To make a number a **perfect square**, every **prime factor** must have an **even power**.

Factorize 2527 → 7 × 19 × 19 = 7¹ × 19².

The prime factor **7** has an odd power (1).

Multiply by **7** to make the power of 7 even (7²).

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ Prime factorization of 2527 = 7 × 19 × 19

⇒ Grouping the factors into pairs: (19 × 19) × 7

⇒ Here, the **prime factor 7** does not have a pair.

⇒ To make it a **perfect square**, we need to multiply by 7.

⇒ New number = 2527 × 7 = 17689 = (133)²

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perfect Square Property

A number is a perfect square if all its prime factors appear an even number of times.

Multiplication/Division Rule

The smallest number to multiply or divide to make a perfect square is the product of all prime factors that have an odd power.

Square Roots of Common Numbers

Recognizing squares like 19² = 361 or 17² = 289 helps in faster prime factorization.</p

questions.question: Three numbers are in the ratio 5 : 4 : 3, and their LCM is 4980. Their HCF is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of numbers = 5 : 4 : 3

Let **HCF** be H. Then **LCM** = H × 5 × 4 × 3

60 × H = 4980

H = 4980 ÷ 60 = 83

**∴ The correct answer is 83.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Ratio = 5 : 4 : 3, **LCM** = 4980

**Formula Used:** **LCM** of numbers (ax, bx, cx) = x × **LCM**(a, b, c), where x is the **HCF**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/453ce1e3f50b1016fd2c9ec61f8a547531dcef286684c0e2723fdae4c04f1dd9.png] 

⇒ Let the numbers be 5x, 4x, and 3x, where x is the **HCF**.

⇒ Since 5, 4, and 3 are **co-prime** to each other (no common factors):

⇒ **LCM**(5x, 4x, 3x) = x × 5 × 4 × 3

⇒ 4980 = 60x

⇒ x = 4980 ÷ 60

⇒ x = 83

**∴ The correct answer is 83.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relationship between LCM and HCF

For two numbers a and b: **Product of numbers** = **HCF** × **LCM**. Note: This rule does not directly apply to more than two numbers.

HCF and Ratio

If the ratio of numbers is a : b : c and **HCF** is H, the numbers are aH, bH, and cH. Their **LCM** is H × LCM(a, b, c).

Co-prime Numbers

If numbers are **co-prime**, their **HCF** is always 1 and their **LCM** is the product of the numbers.</p

questions.question: Where do deleted files go by default in Windows OS?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**The Recycle Bin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **Windows Operating System**, deleted files are temporarily moved to the **Recycle Bin** by default instead of being permanently erased.
 
• This feature allows users to **recover files** that were accidentally deleted.
 
• The **Recycle Bin** acts as a holding area, providing an opportunity to restore items to their original location.
 
• Files in the Recycle Bin remain there until the user decides to **permanently delete** them by emptying the bin or until the storage limit of the bin is reached.
 
• The storage size of the Recycle Bin is typically a **percentage of the total disk space**, and this limit can be customized by the user.
 
• Items in the Recycle Bin retain their original file properties, such as **file type, size, and modification date**, until they are permanently removed.
 
• The Recycle Bin is located on the **desktop interface** of Windows, making it easily accessible to users.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Downloads Folder**__

 __
 
• The **Downloads folder** in Windows OS is a default location where files downloaded from the internet are saved.
 
• It is not associated with deleted files but with **retrieving downloaded content** like documents, videos, or software.
 
• Users can manually move or delete items from the Downloads folder.
 
 
 
• **The Cloud**__
 __
 
• The term **The Cloud** refers to cloud storage services like **Google Drive, OneDrive, or Dropbox**, which are used for storing data online.
 
• Deleted files are not automatically sent to the cloud unless they are synced with a cloud service.
 
• Files stored in the cloud may have their own **recycle bin or trash folder** depending on the service provider.
 
 
 
• **They are permanently erased**__
 
 
• Files in Windows are not permanently erased by default when deleted. They are first moved to the **Recycle Bin**.
 
• However, files can be permanently deleted using **Shift + Delete** or by emptying the Recycle Bin.

questions.question: Which of the following is an incorrect statement about Cache Memory?

options.text: Cache memory is faster than main memory.

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cache memory** is a type of **volatile memory** that provides high-speed data access to the processor.
 
• It is designed to store **frequently accessed data** or instructions so that the processor can retrieve them quickly without accessing slower main memory (RAM).
 
• Cache memory is located **closer to or inside the CPU**, reducing the time taken to fetch data.
 
• Cache memory is significantly **faster than main memory (RAM)**, but it is smaller in size and more expensive.
 
• It is not a form of **secondary storage**. Secondary storage refers to devices like **hard drives, SSDs, and external storage**, which are used for permanent data storage and are slower than both cache and main memory.
 
• The primary goal of cache memory is to **enhance the speed and efficiency** of the CPU by minimizing data access delays.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Cache memory is faster than main memory.**__

 __
 
• **Cache memory** operates at a much higher speed compared to **RAM**, allowing the CPU to process instructions faster.
 
• It uses technologies like **SRAM (Static RAM)**, which is faster than DRAM (used in main memory).
 
 
 
• **Cache memory stores frequently accessed data for quick retrieval.**__
 __
 
• **Cache memory** identifies and temporarily stores **data or instructions** that are frequently used by the CPU.
 
• This minimizes the need to access slower main memory repeatedly, enhancing overall system performance.
 
 
 
• **Cache memory is located close to or inside the CPU.**__
 
 
• Cache memory is either **embedded inside the CPU** (e.g., L1 and L2 cache) or placed **very close to the CPU** (e.g., L3 cache).
 
• This proximity reduces latency, allowing the processor to access data faster.

questions.question: Find the area of a parallelogram, whose base is (3x − 5y + 4) m and height is (x - 5y) m.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Area of Parallelogram** = **Base** × **Height**.

Multiply (3x − 5y + 4) by (x − 5y).

⇒ 3x(x − 5y) − 5y(x − 5y) + 4(x − 5y)

⇒ 3x² − 15xy − 5xy + 25y² + 4x − 20y

⇒ 3x² + 25y² − 20xy + 4x − 20y

**∴ The correct answer is (3x² + 25y² − 20xy + 4x − 20y) m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Base (b)** = (3x − 5y + 4) m

**Height (h)** = (x − 5y) m

**Formula Used:**

**Area of a Parallelogram** = Base × Height

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bb7bad234341248f5a9d1a5d6c3762cdfde7ae1574b8dc2db92af22a6aa2abb0.png]

⇒ Area = (3x − 5y + 4) × (x − 5y)

⇒ Area = 3x(x − 5y) − 5y(x − 5y) + 4(x − 5y)

⇒ Area = (3x × x) − (3x × 5y) − (5y × x) + (5y × 5y) + (4 × x) − (4 × 5y)

⇒ Area = 3x² − 15xy − 5xy + 25y² + 4x − 20y

⇒ Area = 3x² + 25y² − 20xy + 4x − 20y

**∴ The correct answer is (3x² + 25y² − 20xy + 4x − 20y) m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Parallelogram

Opposite sides are equal and parallel. Opposite angles are equal, and diagonals bisect each other.

Perimeter of a Parallelogram

Perimeter = 2 × (sum of adjacent sides) = 2(a + b).

Area using Diagonals

questions.question: The sides (in cm) of a right triangle are (x − 18),(x − 25) and x. Its area (in cm² ) is
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the **Hypotenuse** as the longest side, which is **x**.

The sides must satisfy the **Pythagorean Triplets** logic.

By testing x = 85: Sides are (85 − 18) = 67, (85 − 25) = 60, and 85.

Check: 60² + 61²? No. Test x = 88: Sides are 70, 63, 88. No.

Using **x = 88**: Sides are 70, 63, 88. Test **x = 93**: Sides are 75, 68, 93. No.

Actually, x = 73 gives sides 55, 48, 73. 55² + 48² = 3025 + 2304 = 5329 = 73². Correct.

Area = 1/2 × 55 × 48 = 55 × 24 = 1320.

**∴ The correct answer is 1320 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sides of a **right-angled triangle** are (x − 18), (x − 25), and x.

**Formula Used:** **Pythagoras Theorem**: a² + b² = c² and **Area** = 1/2 × Base × Height.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8bc3f98eb597d4addb3a4314241fa4453fc3fff7e655a8e6d407521f05ab5a85.png] 

⇒ (x − 18)² + (x − 25)² = x²

⇒ (x² − 36x + 324) + (x² − 50x + 625) = x²

⇒ 2x² − 86x + 949 = x²

⇒ x² − 86x + 949 = 0

⇒ x² − 73x − 13x + 949 = 0

⇒ x(x − 73) − 13(x − 73) = 0

⇒ (x − 73)(x − 13) = 0

⇒ x = 73 or x = 13 (But x − 18 and x − 25 must be positive, so x > 25)

⇒ **x = 73**

⇒ Base = 73 − 25 = 48 cm, Height = 73 − 18 = 55 cm

⇒ Area = 1/2 × 48 × 55 = 24 × 55 = 1320 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 1320 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Triplets

Common triplets like (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (7, 24, 25), and (48, 55, 73) help solve right triangle problems quickly without complex algebra.

Right Triangle Area

The area of a right-angled triangle is always half the product of the two sides perpendicular to each other (Base × Height).

Quadratic Roots Selection

Always verify physical dimensions: side lengths must be positive, which often eliminates one of the two roots in a quadratic equation.</p

questions.question: The cost of 4 pens and 5 pencils is ₹193 and the cost of 3 pens and 6 pencils ₹165. The cost of 4 pens and 6 pencils is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equation 1: **4 Pens + 5 Pencils = ₹193**

Equation 2: **3 Pens + 6 Pencils = ₹165** → Dividing by 3 ⇒ **1 Pen + 2 Pencils = ₹55**

Multiply simplified Eq 2 by 4: **4 Pens + 8 Pencils = ₹220**

Difference (3 Pencils) = ₹220 − ₹193 = ₹27 ⇒ **1 Pencil = ₹9**

Required (4 Pens + 6 Pencils) = (4 Pens + 5 Pencils) + 1 Pencil = ₹193 + ₹9 = ₹202

**∴ The correct answer is ₹202.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost of 4 pens and 5 pencils = ₹193

Cost of 3 pens and 6 pencils = ₹165

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/67fc47d70ccc1ada6c2eb3f290257da60c94c7c5481d93bb92f3f1800960266a.png] 

Let the cost of one pen be **x** and the cost of one pencil be **y**.

⇒ 4x + 5y = 193 --- (i)

⇒ 3x + 6y = 165 --- (ii)

From (ii), divide by 3:

⇒ x + 2y = 55 ⇒ x = 55 − 2y

Substitute **x** in (i):

⇒ 4(55 − 2y) + 5y = 193

⇒ 220 − 8y + 5y = 193

⇒ 220 − 3y = 193

⇒ 3y = 27 ⇒ **y = 9**

Substitute **y** in the equation for **x**:

⇒ x = 55 − 2(9) = 55 − 18 = **37**

Now, find the cost of 4 pens and 6 pencils:

⇒ 4x + 6y = 4(37) + 6(9)

⇒ 148 + 54 = 202

**∴ The correct answer is ₹202.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simultaneous Linear Equations

These are equations with multiple variables solved together using **substitution** or **elimination** methods to find unique values.

Unitary Method

The technique of finding the value of a **single unit** and then multiplying by the required number of units to get the total cost.

Cost Price Calculation

Total Cost = (Number of Items 1 × Rate 1) + (Number of Items 2 × Rate 2).

Remaining work = 528 − 150 = **378 units**.

Remaining time taken by (B+C) = 378 ÷ (16 + 11) = 378 ÷ 27 = **14 days**.

questions.question: At what rate of interest per annum will a sum of ₹1,000 amount to ₹1,728 in 1 year and 6 months, if the interest is compounded half-yearly?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Principal (P)** = ₹1,000, **Amount (A)** = ₹1,728, **Time (t)** = 1.5 years = 3 half-years.

Ratio of A : P = 1728 : 1000.

For 3 periods, take the **cube root**: √³(1728) : √³(1000) = 12 : 10.

Half-yearly rate = [(12 − 10) ÷ 10] × 100 = 20%.

Annual Rate = 20% × 2 = 40%.

**∴ The correct answer is 40%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹1,000

**Amount (A)** = ₹1,728

**Time (T)** = 1 year 6 months = 1.5 years

**Compounding:** Half-yearly ⇒ Number of periods (n) = 1.5 × 2 = 3

**Formula Used:** A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ, where r is the **half-yearly interest rate**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/60f5231a74da4bac7c60fc7f4cd802219f59f0b139fd9866f2f6e131d28ea89d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 1728 = 1000(1 + r/100)³

⇒ 1728 ÷ 1000 = (1 + r/100)³

⇒ 1.728 = (1 + r/100)³

⇒ √³(1.728) = 1 + r/100

⇒ 1.2 = 1 + r/100

⇒ r/100 = 0.2

⇒ r = 20% (Half-yearly rate)

⇒ **Annual Rate of Interest** = 2 × r = 2 × 20%

⇒ Annual Rate = 40%

**∴ The correct answer is 40%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Half-Yearly Compounding Rule

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the **annual rate** is divided by 2 (R/2) and the **time** in years is multiplied by 2 (2n).

Quarterly Compounding Rule

When interest is compounded quarterly, the **annual rate** is divided by 4 (R/4) and the **time** is multiplied by 4 (4n).

Effective Rate of Interest

It is the actual annual interest rate when compounding occurs more than once a year, calculated as: Effective Rate = [1 + (R/n)]ⁿ − 1.

questions.question: Which Greek ambassador visited the court of Chandragupta Maurya?

__
 
• **Megasthenes** was a **Greek ambassador** who visited the court of **Chandragupta Maurya**, the founder of the Maurya Empire in India.
 
• He served as an envoy of the **Seleucid Emperor Seleucus I Nicator**, who sent him to establish diplomatic relations with the Mauryan Empire.
 
• Megasthenes is best known for his work, **Indica**, which is a detailed account of Indian society, geography, culture, and governance during the Mauryan period.
 
• His writings provide valuable insights into the Mauryan administration, including the functioning of the **capital city Pataliputra**, the use of a well-organized bureaucracy, and the king's role in governance.
 
• Megasthenes described the Indian caste system, the way of life of the people, and the flora and fauna of India, which were considered unique by the Greeks.
 
• The information provided by Megasthenes serves as one of the earliest foreign accounts of India and helps historians reconstruct the history of ancient India.

questions.question: The median of the observations 21, 36, 73, 71, 35, 38, 49, 37, 26, 66 and 73 is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Arrange the given 11 observations in **ascending order**:

21, 26, 35, 36, 37, **38**, 49, 66, 71, 73, 73

Since the number of observations (n = 11) is **odd**, the median is the ((n + 1) ÷ 2)th term.

**Median** = 6th term = **38**.

**∴ The correct answer is 38.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Observations: 21, 36, 73, 71, 35, 38, 49, 37, 26, 66, 73

Total number of observations (n) = **11**

**Formula Used:**

When n is odd, **Median** = Value of ((n + 1) ÷ 2)th observation after sorting in ascending order.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cef873fab24d8236fd16e0f116262d64037022ed8f7af89e581b8a75db1fadc6.png] 

**Calculations:**

First, arrange the given observations in ascending order:

⇒ 21, 26, 35, 36, 37, 38, 49, 66, 71, 73, 73

Count the total number of observations:

⇒ n = 11

Since n is odd, the median is calculated as:

⇒ Median = ((11 + 1) ÷ 2)th observation

⇒ Median = 6th observation

Looking at the sorted list, the 6th observation is **38**.

Let us verify why the other options are incorrect:

⇒ **Option (2) 35** is the 3rd observation, which is not the middle term.

⇒ **Option (3) 37** is the 5th observation, which is just before the middle term.

⇒ **Option (4) 36** is the 4th observation, which is not the middle term.

**∴ The correct answer is 38.**

**__Additional Information__**

Median for Even Number of Observations

If the number of observations (n) is even, the median is the average of the (n ÷ 2)th and ((n ÷ 2) + 1)th observations. Formula: Median = [Value of (n/2)th term + Value of (n/2 + 1)th term] ÷ 2.

Mean (Arithmetic Average)

The sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations. Formula: Mean = (Σ xᵢ) ÷ n.

Mode

The value that appears most frequently in a data set. In the given data set, 73 appears twice, so the mode is 73.

Empirical Relationship

The relationship between Mean, Median, and Mode for moderately skewed distributions is given by: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.</p

questions.question: A boat takes 76 minutes to go 32.2 km upstream. The ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to that of the stream is 9 : 8. How much approximate total time (in hours) will the boat take to go 44.9 km upstream and 57.8 km downstream?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Speed of Boat (u)** : **Speed of Stream (v)** = 9 : 8.

**Upstream speed (u−v)** = 9x − 8x = 1x; **Downstream speed (u+v)** = 9x + 8x = 17x.

Current Upstream speed = 32.2 km ÷ (76/60) h = 25.42 kmph ⇒ x ≈ 25.42.

Total time = (44.9 ÷ x) + (57.8 ÷ 17x) = (44.9 ÷ 25.42) + (57.8 ÷ 432.14) ≈ 1.76 + 0.13 = 1.89 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.9 hours.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cd836bdb0a858fa497fd6f7e90e8fe0a80b26c8bd012a411f509bb5c152187e4.png] 

**Given:** Upstream Distance = 32.2 km, Time = 76 min, Ratio u:v = 9:8.

**Formula Used:** Speed = Distance ÷ Time; Upstream = u − v; Downstream = u + v.

⇒ Upstream speed (sᵤ) = 32.2 ÷ (76/60) = 32.2 × 15 / 19 = 25.421 kmph.

⇒ Let u = 9x and v = 8x. Upstream speed = 9x − 8x = x.

⇒ ∴ x = 25.421 kmph.

⇒ Downstream speed (sd) = 9x + 8x = 17x = 17 × 25.421 = 432.157 kmph.

⇒ Time for 44.9 km Upstream = 44.9 ÷ 25.421 ≈ 1.766 hours.

⇒ Time for 57.8 km Downstream = 57.8 ÷ 432.157 ≈ 0.133 hours.

⇒ Total Time = 1.766 + 0.133 = 1.899 hours ≈ 1.9 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.9 hours.**

**__Additional Information__**

Upstream and Downstream Speeds

If **u** is boat speed in still water and **v** is stream speed, then Upstream Speed = u − v and Downstream Speed = u + v.

Average Speed of Boat

For the same distance D, Average Speed = (Upstream × Downstream) ÷ Still Water Speed.

Speed Conversion

To convert kmph to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert minutes to hours, divide by 60.</p
